title: Time and tempo-synchronized divisions
text: Delay has separate left/right delay lines. Sync selects sixteenth-note divisions; selection 4 denotes four sixteenths, one quarter note. Offset shortens timing at negative values and extends it at positive values. Time mode offers 1.00 ms to 5.00 s. These are documented units/range, not sample rounding or tempo-change rules.

title: Stereo Link and independent offsets
text: With Stereo Link on, changing one delay time applies to both channels, but each Offset remains independently adjustable. Linking initial unequal values, unlink restoration and simultaneous edits are unresolved.

title: Feedback paths
text: Feedback returns each channel output to its own delay input; with Ping Pong off the documented feedback loops do not feed the opposite channel. Feedback gain law, runaway limit and saturation remain U.

title: Freeze admission and buffer cycling
text: Freeze endlessly cycles the audio already in the buffer and ignores new input until deactivated. This does not establish a capture length, crossfade, exact periodic output or buffer persistence across save/reset.

title: Input band-pass filter
text: The switchable band-pass filter precedes the delay signal. The display X-axis and Freq slider adjust center frequency; Y-axis and Width slider adjust bandwidth. Its transfer function is U.

title: Modulation targets and section visibility
text: An LFO modulates delay time and filter frequency through separate Delay and Filter depth sliders. LFO Controls expands the collapsed section; the documented initial display is collapsed. The timing smoothing mode can change the sonic result of modulation. No default values or oscillator phase are established for the pinned build.

title: LFO modes, shapes and Morph
text: Rate offers Rate, Time, Synced, Triplet, Dotted and Sixteenth modes. Wave offers Sine, Triangle, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Square, S&H and Wander, with Morph shaping the selected wave. During playback the LED flashes with current LFO rate. Random distributions and phase resets are U.

title: Timing transitions
text: Repitch produces a pitch change when delay time changes; Fade crossfades old/new times; Jump changes time immediately and can click during an existing decay. Repitch is the manual-described initial mode, with exact-build defaults U. No smoothing duration or requirement to click is inferred.

title: Ping Pong
text: Ping Pong makes the delay signal alternate between left and right channels. Input summing, initial side, stereo normalization and interaction with Link are U.

title: Dry/Wet
text: Dry/Wet balances dry and processed audio; 100% is documented for a return so that only processed signal is output. No bit-exact dry bypass, latency or mix equation follows.

title: Hi-Quality context option
text: Hi-Quality is available through the device context/Show Options menu. It improves delay interpolation in Repitch/Fade and applies tape-style timing smoothing in Repitch. Numerical interpolation, cost and behavior in Jump are U.

title: Equal-Loudness context option
text: Dry/Wet - Equal-Loudness changes between linear and equal-loudness output behavior; enabled 50/50 is described as equally loud for most signals. This qualitative statement is not an equal-power coefficient formula or loudness guarantee for correlated signals.

title: Channel modes
text: Echo provides Stereo, Ping Pong and Mid/Side. Mid/Side replaces the Left/Right delay controls with Mid/Side controls. No matrix normalization or sample-level stereo trajectory is specified.

title: Delay units and Sync Mode
text: Delay time is in beat divisions with Sync on and milliseconds with Sync off. Notes, Triplet, Dotted and 16th are selectable Sync Modes; changing Sync Mode affects sound only while Sync is on.

title: Stereo Link and offsets
text: Stereo Link propagates time, Sync-switch and Sync-Mode edits to both delay lines; Offset remains independent per line. The initial value chosen on linking is U.

title: Input gain and dry distortion
text: Input adjusts gain applied to the dry signal; D applies distortion to it. The distortion curve, clipping threshold and gain location beyond this description remain U.

title: Feedback and inversion
text: Feedback returns each channel output to delay inputs; Ø inverts output before feeding it back. This documents sign inversion, not a full gain/stability law or parity of the first repeat.

title: Echo Tunnel
text: Echo Tunnel displays repeats progressing outside to center; spacing denotes repeat interval, white dots form a fixed eighth-note reference. Dragging the display edits delay times.

title: Filters and display
text: Filter enables high-pass and low-pass filtering; each has cutoff and resonance. The triangle shows/hides the Filter Display, whose points also edit filters. Transfer functions, ordering beyond the manual and transition behavior are U.

title: LFO wave, rate and phase
text: The Modulation tab offers sine, triangle, saw up, saw down, square and noise. Sync selects beat-based Rate versus Freq in Hz. Display dragging edits frequency; Phase offsets left/right waveforms and 180 degrees denotes opposed phase. Exact wave shapes/noise law are U.

title: Modulation targets and x4
text: Mod Delay targets delay time, Modulation x4 multiplies delay-modulation depth by four, and Mod Filter targets the filter. This does not establish a time-domain equation after clipping or smoothing.

title: Envelope versus LFO source
text: Env Mix blends the LFO and envelope follower: 0% selects LFO only and 100% envelope only. Envelope detection, attack/release and blending law are U.

title: Input gate and wet ducking
text: Gate operates at the input and mutes components below Threshold; Release sets closing time after a drop below threshold. Ducking reduces wet signal while input exceeds its Threshold, with Release after it drops. Equality, detector curve, attenuation amount, sidechain topology and exact timing are U.

title: Noise and Wobble
text: Noise adds vintage-character noise with Amount and Morph. Wobble adds irregular delay-time modulation with Amount and Morph. Random processes, seed, spectral law and restart continuity are U.

title: Repitch versus crossfade
text: Repitch on produces pitch variation when delay time changes; off crossfades old/new times. No fade duration, resampling kernel or state reset is specified.

title: Idle shutdown exception
text: Any application-observable consequence of the documented idle shutdown and Noise+Gate exception remains unknown. No shutdown indicator, CPU criterion, tail cutoff or internal processing mechanism is required; the manual statement is research context only.

title: Reverb placement and decay
text: Reverb adjusts added reverberation; Location offers pre delay, post delay and within feedback. Decay lengthens/shortens reverb tail; its kernel and numerical tail are U.

title: Stereo width, output and mix
text: Stereo acts on wet width: 0% is mono, above 100% is widened. Output changes processed gain. Dry/Wet balances dry/processed signals and 100% is intended for returns. Equal-Loudness is a Dry/Wet context option; its 50/50 loudness statement applies to most signals and establishes no coefficients.

title: Three delay inputs and output panning
text: Three independently enabled delay lines have input selections left, left+right and right respectively. Each output normally uses its source channel; its Pan can override output placement. Input summing/normalization, disabled-line tail and pan law remain U.

title: Filters and feedback routing
text: Linked low/high-pass filtering precedes each delay and is also in its feedback path. Each filter has its own switch. X adjusts band frequency and Y bandwidth. A filter bypass is distinct from disabling its entire line.

title: Sync and fractional timing
text: Sync expresses time as sixteenth divisions; 4 denotes a quarter note. Percentage adjustment shortens/extends delay fractions in Sync. A displayed number does not define fractional-sample conversion.

title: Milliseconds editing
text: Sync off uses milliseconds. Delay Time can be edited by vertical drag or typed value. Accepted numerical range, out-of-range parsing, precision and smoothing remain U.

title: Feedback
text: Each Feedback control sets returned output amount. Very high values may produce runaway oscillation; the manual gives no safe maximum, limiter, exact gain or guaranteed finite tail.

title: Line levels and Dry
text: Each delay has a volume control offering up to +6 dB. Dry adjusts unprocessed level; minimum is documented for return use. These are independent levels, not a Dry/Wet ratio.

title: Grains and Frequency
text: Grain Delay divides input into individually delayed grains that may change pitch. Frequency determines grain size/duration and changes how Pitch and Spray sound. Exact grain schedule/window/overlap and Frequency-to-duration law are U.

title: X/Y assignments
text: Parameter rows assign X below the display and Y at its left. Delay Time can be assigned to X; Dry/Wet can be assigned to Y. Pointer mapping and assignment persistence remain U.

title: Synchronized delay and milliseconds
text: Sync selects sixteenth divisions with 4 equal to a quarter note and percentage timing adjustment. Sync off selects milliseconds, editable by vertical drag or typing. Randomized grain timing does not establish exact output onset at this nominal delay.

title: Spray random delay
text: Spray adds random delay changes; low/high descriptions indicate temporal smearing through disruption of source rhythm. No distribution, maximum offset, seed, replay identity or monotonic audio metric is established.

title: Pitch and Random Pitch
text: Pitch transposes grains; Random Pitch varies individual-grain pitches and interacts with Pitch. The pitch-shift method, random distribution, tuning precision and no-op bit identity are U.

title: Feedback and dry/wet
text: Feedback returns output to the delay input; high values may run away without a documented bound. Dry/wet balances dry and processed audio and can be assigned to Y. The mix law and random-state behavior in feedback are U.

title: Input filters
text: Input first passes through individually switchable low/high cut filters. X controls band center, Y bandwidth; sliders offer the same controls. Cutoff laws, slope and bypass transition are U.

title: Early reflections and Spin
text: Early reflections precede the diffuse tail. Spin modulates early reflections with Amount and Rate and can be disabled. Large rates may cause Doppler shifts/panning; no trajectory or threshold is specified.

title: Shape
text: At smaller Shape values early reflections decay more gradually and diffuse onset is sooner, increasing overlap. Larger values yield quicker reflection decay and later diffuse onset. No continuous mapping or exact onset/decay metric follows.

title: Diffuse tail and shelving
text: The Diffusion Network generates the tail. Independent high/low shelving filters shape frequency-dependent decay and can be turned off. Filter transfer, decay multipliers and frequency equality are U.

title: Diffusion and Scale
text: Diffusion and Scale control tail density/coarseness, with pronounced coloration at extremely small room Size. No delay-line topology or parameter law is established.

title: Chorus
text: Chorus modulates the diffusion with Amount and Rate and has an independent disable switch. Exact oscillator phases, waves and reset state are U.

title: Predelay
text: Predelay is in milliseconds before the first early reflection. The manual describes 1-25 ms as typical natural-room choices; this is not its allowed range or rounding rule.

title: Size and Smooth
text: Size controls virtual room volume. Smooth None changes diffusion delay times immediately; Slow/Fast update them over a period. Exact periods, interpolation and transition ordering are U.

title: Decay definition
text: Decay denotes time for tail amplitude to fall to 1/1000 of its initial amplitude (-60 dB). This defines the documented quantity, not a calibrated output crossing in a multiband/modulated signal, finite tail termination or a numerical exponential.

title: Freeze, Flat and Cut
text: Freeze sustains the diffuse response almost endlessly. With Freeze on, Flat bypasses high/low shelves; Flat off permits energy loss in attenuated bands according to shelf state. Cut prevents new input contributing to frozen reverberation; Cut off admits it. No exact infinite tail or bypass law outside Freeze follows.

title: Stereo, Density and output
text: Stereo lowest setting mixes output to mono; 120 degrees describes independent reverberant channels. Density trades quality/performance, with Sparse and High named endpoints. Reflect and Diffuse independently scale their components; Dry/Wet balances overall dry/wet. No coefficient matrix, CPU count or mix law is specified.

title: Wet send and predelay
text: Send changes gain feeding reverb while leaving dry signal unaffected. Predelay offers time/beat-synced units; each mode has an independent Feedback setting. These are distinct from the algorithm additional Delay. Timing units, feedback persistence across mode toggles and sample conversion need separate evidence.

title: Serial routing
text: Serial sends convolution output into the algorithm engine. The convolution stays active; Blend 100/0 gives convolution-only output, while 0/100 gives algorithmic output fed by convolution. It is not raw-input algorithm-only at the second endpoint. The interpolation law is U.

title: Parallel routing
text: Parallel keeps convolution and algorithm engines separate. Blend 100/0 gives pure convolution and 0/100 pure algorithmic output. Exact summation/gain law is U.

title: Single-engine routing and disabled controls
text: Algorithm uses only the algorithm engine; Convolution only convolution. Unused-engine controls are grayed out. Blend has no effect in either single-engine route. Stored hidden values, CPU behavior and sample-identical no-op output are U.

title: IR selection and display
text: Category and IR selectors choose impulses; arrows advance continuously across category boundaries. Waveform reflects Attack/Decay/Size changes. Ten documented categories are Early Reflections, Real Places, Chambers and Large Rooms, Made for Drums, Halls, Plates, Springs, Bigger Spaces, Textures and User. Exact installed IR list/version is U.

title: User IR import and removal
text: Dropping an audio file on the waveform adds it as an IR; audio siblings in its folder are also added. Remove the device and add it again: previously added User samples no longer appear in User until added again. This does not define saved-Set restoration, supported codec set, recursion, file sorting or cleanup of source bytes.

title: Convolution envelope
text: Attack/Decay control the IR amplitude envelope attack/decay times; Size controls relative IR size. Exact envelope, resampling, normalization, latency and stereo-channel convolution are U.

title: Algorithms and common controls
text: Algorithms are Dark Hall, Quartz, Shimmer, Tides and Prism, with controls changing by selection. All have Decay, Size, Delay and Freeze. Decay denotes approximate time to -60 dB, Size virtual room size and Delay an additional algorithmic predelay in milliseconds. No exact kernel, sample delay or tolerance is established.

title: Freeze versus Freeze In
text: Freeze blocks input to the algorithmic engine and sets decay to infinite for sustained output. Freeze In adds new input to frozen reverberation. This contract is algorithmic; it does not establish freezing convolution output, state persistence or numerical infinite duration.

title: Dark Hall controls
text: Dark Hall provides Damping for high-frequency filtering, Mod for tail movement, Shape from small/resonant toward large/diffused, Bass X low-tail crossover and Bass Mult low-tail decay scaling. Long decay with tiny Size can give gong-like resonance; no guaranteed timbre or crossover law follows.

title: Quartz controls
text: Quartz provides Damping (high filtering), Lo Damp (low filtering), Mod (tail movement), Diffusion (sparse to dense) and Distance (closer/denser to farther/more-spaced reflections). No monotonic waveform statistic or exact reflection schedule is specified.

title: Shimmer controls and zero amount
text: Shimmer includes Damping, Mod, Diffusion, Pitch in semitones and Shimmer amount. Pitch-shifted feedback creates rising/falling tails; Shimmer=0% applies no pitch shifting and increasing amount makes pitched signal more present. Size affects spacing of echoes on percussive material. No resampling, diffusion threshold kernel or feedback stability law is specified.

title: Tides modulation
text: Tides modulates output spectrum with a multiband filter. Damping controls high filtering; Tide controls texture intensity; Wave morphs noise (0%) to sine (50%) to square (100%); Phase=180 degrees opposes left/right modulation; Rate uses beat divisions with Triplet/16th/Dotted variations. Random spectra and phase/timing precision are U.

title: Prism band decay controls
text: Prism is described as based on spectrally flat velvet noise. Low Mult and High Mult scale respective tail-band decays; X over sets the band boundary. Noise process, crossover filters, gain normalization and exact decay curves are U.

title: EQ placement and enable
text: EQ has its own tab and toggle. The documented usual position follows both engines; Pre Algo places it before the algorithm engine regardless of selected reverb routing. This text does not resolve every Convolution-only inactive-algorithm topology or changing-tail transition.

title: EQ bands
text: Four EQ bands include low/high bands switchable between pass filters and shelves, with 6 to 96 dB/octave slope range in pass modes; two middle peak bands cover the frequency range. Exact band domains, slope menu steps, cutoff/Q and digital transfer functions are U.

title: Wet width and Dry/Wet
text: Stereo controls wet width with mono at 0% and widening above 100%; Dry/Wet balances processed/dry audio and 100% is documented for return use. No mono matrix, pan gain or mixing formula is established.

title: Vintage
text: Vintage increasingly emulates lower sample rates/bit depths, with four presets Subtle, Old, Older and Extreme. No actual sample rates, bit depths, noise shaping or exact distortion is established.

title: Bass Mono
text: Bass Mono converts frequencies below 180 Hz of the described output signal to mono. The source does not settle dry-path participation, crossover transition/filter slopes, equality at 180 Hz or channel summation coefficients.

title: Five resonators and mode
text: Five parallel resonators add tonal character. Mode A and B select distinct resonance modes; descriptions of realistic/low-pitched effects establish no modal kernel or numerical equivalence.

title: Input filter
text: Input filtering precedes resonators, with low-pass, band-pass, high-pass and notch types, and Frequency controlling selected filter frequency. Filter order, slope and switching tails are U.

title: Decay, Const and Color
text: Decay changes resonator sustain; normal pitch-dependent decay lasts longer at lower notes. Const selects pitch-independent decay; Color controls brightness. Exact time definition, frequency law, equality and spectrum are U.

title: Channel assignments
text: Resonator I receives left+right, II/IV left only, III/V right only. Summation scaling and the output stereo matrix are U.

title: Root tuning and context
text: Without scale awareness/tuning, I sets root and others follow musical intervals. With scale awareness, I is relative to active clip scale in octave 2; others relative to I. With tuning active, I uses an absolute tuning-defined pitch and others relative to it. Exact tuning precedence, no-active-clip fallback and changes during a tail remain U.

title: Note, Fine and relative ranges
text: Default Note is semitones C-1 to C5; scale awareness changes to scale degrees, tuning to note indices. Fine I edits cents. II-V transpose relative to I by ±24 semitones or ±21 scale degrees and have individual Fine controls. Note-label ranges do not establish internal numbering, quantization or frequency calculation.

title: Independent enable and gain
text: Every resonator has On/Off and Gain. Turning I off leaves others active; a disabled resonator is described as consuming no CPU, but this is not an application CPU benchmark or silence/tail oracle.

title: Wet width, gain and balance
text: Width acts only on wet output and at 0% blends II-V to mono. Gain adjusts resonated level unless Dry/Wet=0%. Dry/Wet balances paths. No claim is made that I stereo mapping is determined by the II-V statement.

title: Tabs and engine color roles
text: Hybrid Reverb has Reverb and EQ tabs; Reverb contains controls for both engines. Convolution controls are described as yellow and algorithm controls as blue. These are named visible roles, not a required RGB/pixel palette, layout geometry, default selected tab or signal-processing result.
